newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hansol, Yu Sung news seen as drag on Seoul shares.
newsitem.headline: Hansol, Yu Sung news seen as drag on Seoul shares.

text.p: South Korean stocks are expected to fall on Wednesday, dragged down by unrelated news about the Hansol Group and Yu Sung Co, brokers said.
The Chosun Ilbo reported on Wednesday the Hansol Group, whose listed affiliates number seven, had managed seven billion won on behalf of an associate of President Kim Young-sam's son.
A public information official at the group said on Wednesday Hansol officials were discussing the news.
Textile maker Yu Sung said on Tuesday it defaulted on repayments of promissory notes and would seek court protection.
The composite index fell 3.30 points to 701.57 on Tuesday.
The Korea Stock Exchange said on late Tuesday trading in Yu Sung's shares would be suspended indefinitely from Wednesday.
It last traded up 100 won at 11,600 on Tuesday.
"These stories will seriously affect the overall mood, not only shares of the companies directly involved," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
Hansol's listed affiliates are Hansol Paper, Hansol Telecommunication, Hansol Chemical, Hansol Electron, Hansol Merchant Bank, Hansol CSN Hansol Paperboard.
